title: Reading and writing user files safely
when: The desktop app saves user documents and must never leave a half written or corrupted file after a crash, a full disk or a bad path.
prompt:
Goal: files.js reads and writes user files with atomic saves, a backup copy, size limits and clear errors.
Steps:
1. Atomic save: write to path + ".tmp", read it back and compare length, then Neutralino.filesystem.move(tmp, path) to replace the original.
2. Before replacing, copy the old file to path + ".bak" with Neutralino.filesystem.copy; keep one backup.
3. Before reading call Neutralino.filesystem.getStats(path); refuse files over 50 MB with a message instead of freezing.
4. Read text as UTF-8; strip a leading BOM (\uFEFF); keep the original line endings and write them back the same way.
5. Parse JSON in try/catch; on failure offer to open the .bak copy.
6. Paths from the app (recent list, settings) must stay inside expected folders: reject values containing ".." segments after normalizing.
7. Map errors to text: NE_FS_FILRDER (cannot read), NE_FS_FILWRER (cannot write), and a full disk message.
8. Never write into the app install folder; it can be read only.
Quality bar:
- Killing the app mid save leaves the old or the new file, never a mix.
- The user always sees which file failed.
Pitfalls:
- Writing straight over the original file.
- Reading binary files as text and saving them back broken.
Verify:
- [ ] Saves go through a .tmp file and a move.
- [ ] JSON parsing is guarded.
- [ ] Large files are refused before reading.
Output: files.js and its use in doc.js.

examples.input: o app travou salvando e o arquivo do cliente corrompeu
examples.output: Atomic save via .tmp then move, one .bak copy, 50 MB guard, BOM handling, mapped error codes
